names.name: Īśvara, the Lord dwelling in the heart of all beings (18.61)
Vāsudeva, Keśava, Hari, Kṛṣṇa the lord of yoga (18.74–78)

descriptions: the one from whom beings proceed and by whom all this is pervaded, to be worshipped with one's own work (18.46)
one imperishable being seen by sāttvic knowledge in all beings, undivided among the divided (18.20)
the Lord in the heart who makes all beings revolve by his māyā as if mounted on a machine (18.61)
known in truth by devotion — how great and who he is — and entered (18.55)
relation_to_self: BhG 16–18: the Lord dwells in the bodies of all (16.18, 17.6) and in the heart of all beings (18.61); the one who has become brahman attains supreme devotion to him, knows him in truth and enters him (18.54–55).
relation_to_world: BhG 16–18: all this is pervaded by him and beings proceed from him (18.46); he moves all beings by his māyā (18.61); the demonic deny that the world has a Lord (16.8).
